A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable main text, two tables, eight figures, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and figure-placement changes.

before.justification: v1.pdf synthesizes prior research without reporting original empirical results. Its tables classify methods and surveys, Appendix A describes literature selection, and Appendix G provides illustrative applications.

after.justification: v2.pdf remains a literature survey without original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses. The added citations do not introduce results produced by this work.

M1.justification: The sequential, triage-based, and joint cooperation categories and their described procedures remain unchanged. Additional citations introduce no proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets or tasks. Technology-assisted document review is added as a cited application in Section 3.1, not as an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed system. Tables 1–2 retain the same descriptive comparisons of cooperation categories and prior surveys.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocol is introduced or revised. Section 4.1 retains its proposal for a future comprehensive benchmark, and Appendix A's literature-selection procedure is unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are added or removed. Appendix G retains the same illustrative data-annotation and information-seeking applications.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests for original results. Section 4.1's discussion of human uncertainty estimation remains unchanged.

E6.justification: No numerical performance results or empirical findings are added or revised. Appendix A retains the counts of 1,007 identified papers and 147 selected papers; existing application examples and qualitative summaries are preserved.

T1.justification: Appendix C retains the same participant and action definitions, constraints, policies, shared-utility optimization, and independent-action formulation. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reviewing cooperation principles and formalizations, proposing a unified taxonomy, and identifying research frontiers.

C2.justification: Appendix F shifts its trust argument from absent human involvement in model-model cooperation specifically to NLP-model predictions generally. This modestly revises the argument's applicability; the medical examples and substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A's search keywords and selection description are retained. No implementation settings, hardware information, reproducibility instructions, or code/data access disclosures are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Cormack and Grossman (2014, 2016) and Lewis et al. (2021) for technology-assisted document review, plus Zhang et al. (2025) on programmer attention. Other reference changes update existing works' publication details; the main novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2.pdf corrects 'trial-based' to 'triage-based' in Section 4.1, makes small wording and capitalization edits, updates affiliations and correspondence text, and adds acknowledgments. The narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, Figure 4 moves from the left to the right column, and appendix figures are repositioned, including Figure 8 moving to the final page. All eight figures and both tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2.pdf modestly improves literature coverage through the added document-review references, corrects confusing terminology in Section 4.1, and enlarges Figure 1 for readability. Updated bibliographic details improve source identification. These gains are limited because the central taxonomy, formalization, and substantive discussion remain largely unchanged.
